core_obligations: Reduce to a strictly perfect witness and truncate it (proof lines 12782-12790): after passing to a covering and localising, choose a strictly perfect complex E^bullet with a map alpha to E inducing isomorphisms on cohomology in degrees >= a, and replace E^bullet by its truncation sigma_{>= a-1}.

Identify the cone (proof lines 12791-12799): from the distinguished triangle E^bullet -> E -> C -> E^bullet[1], the vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of E and E^bullet together with the properties of alpha give C = K[2-a] with K = Ker(E^{a-1} -> E^a).

Compute the relevant Tor and deduce flatness (proof lines 12800-12811): tensoring with an arbitrary O-module F, the tor-amplitude assumption on E in [a, b] forces K tensor F -> E^{a-1} tensor F to have image the kernel of the map to E^a tensor F, hence Tor_1(E', F) = 0 for E' = Coker(E^{a-1} -> E^a); the flatness criterion makes E' flat.

Conclude perfection (proof lines 12812-12815): there is a covering {U_i -> U} over which E' is a direct summand of a finite free module, and the complex E' -> E^{a+1} -> ... -> E^b restricted to U_i is quasi-isomorphic to E, so E is perfect.
proof_roadmap: Localise to get a strictly perfect witness and truncate it below degree a.
Read the cone of the witness as a shift of the kernel K of the degree a-1 to a map.

Use tor-amplitude in [a, b] to see that the degree-a cokernel E' has vanishing first Tor, hence is flat, hence locally a summand of a finite free module; the truncated complex is then a bounded finite strictly perfect representative of E.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the precise criterion for perfection: tor amplitude in a bounded interval plus (a-1)-pseudo-coherence implies perfect (statement lines 12773-12779). Its content is the flatness of the degree-a cokernel (proof lines 12782-12811): after localising to a strictly perfect witness and truncating, one identifies the cone of the witness as a shift of the kernel K, computes that Tor_1 of the cokernel E' vanishes using the tor-amplitude in [a, b], applies the flatness criterion, and finally uses that a flat module of finite presentation is locally a direct summand of a finite free module. H2: one localisation, one cone computation and one flatness deduction, all written out.
